overall_diagnosis: The failures are concentrated in core spreadsheet-authoring quality: required ranges/cells were left empty (PWT labor series in column C), verifier-critical formulas were missing (HP-filter objective in the expected objective cell), and at least one key parameter evaluated to the wrong type (depreciation rate stored/evaluated as text, triggering TypeErrors). Prior recalculation also produced many formula errors (#NAME?, #DIV/0!), indicating use of non-portable/unsupported Excel functions or unguarded calculations. These issues violate the xlsx skill’s requirements around correct formula construction, evaluator compatibility, numeric outputs, and zero formula errors.

diagnosed_skills.diagnosis: Workbook outputs were not fully populated and not test-compatible: missing PWT!C labor values, missing HP-filter objective formula in the expected cell, and Production!B3 evaluating as text rather than a numeric value. Additionally, widespread #NAME?/#DIV/0! during recalc suggests unsupported functions (in the checker’s Excel engine) and/or unguarded denominators. The current skill guidance under-specifies (1) verifying required ranges are non-empty, (2) ensuring verifier-checked cells contain formulas that evaluate numerically, (3) using a conservative function set for compatibility, and (4) running an explicit pre-submit error audit until zero formula errors.
diagnosed_skills.repair_instruction:
Update xlsx/SKILL.md with benchmark-oriented spreadsheet QA and compatibility rules:
1) Required-range completeness: before submission, confirm all specified source/input series ranges are populated with numeric values (e.g., PWT columns B/C across the checked rows); forbid leaving blanks/placeholders in verifier-checked ranges.
2) Verifier-critical cells: explicitly require that all named/expected objective/parameter cells (e.g., HP-filter objective cell, depreciation-rate cell) contain formulas (or fixed numeric values) that evaluate to finite numerics without needing manual Solver execution.
3) Numeric type enforcement: add a rule that any cell used in numeric comparisons must be numeric (not stored as text). Provide coercion patterns: VALUE(x), --x, N(x); avoid quoting numbers; align number formats but prioritize stored type.
4) Compatibility function set: warn against functions that can produce #NAME? in alternate evaluators (e.g., LET/LAMBDA/XLOOKUP/dynamic arrays unless explicitly allowed). Prefer broadly supported constructs (INDEX/MATCH, SUMPRODUCT, IF/IFERROR, OFFSET only if necessary, LN/EXP, TREND).
5) Zero-error process: mandate a final full recalc + scan for #NAME?/#DIV/0!/#REF!/#VALUE!/#N/A; fix by guarding denominators, using IFERROR where appropriate, and ensuring no required inputs are blank—iterate until zero formula errors.
